note: Relapsed/refractory FL treated with PI3Kδ-selective inhibitors (idelalisib, zandelisib, linperlisib): the class went into patients on ex-vivo patient B cells and B-cell lines with no FL animal model, the p110δ kinase-dead mouse foretold the immune colitis, and the 2016 infection deaths and 2022 withdrawals were trial-design and class-safety events rather than model failures.
label: Follicular lymphoma (PI3Kδ)

engagement.model: Patient B-cell tumour samples and B-cell lines ex vivo
engagement.note: CAL-101 (idelalisib) cut constitutive pAkt and triggered apoptosis in B-cell lines and primary patient samples; the read-out carried forward was pAkt and BCR-driven chemokines.
engagement.short: CAL-101 cuts pAkt in patient B cells
engagement.quote: CAL-101 blocked constitutive phosphatidylinositol-3-kinase signaling, resulting in decreased phosphorylation of Akt and other downstream effectors, an increase in poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase and caspase cleavage and an induction of apoptosis.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the FDA pharmacology review (NDA 205858) describes the same assays, including 86% pAKT inhibition at 0.1 µM in biopsy B cells from 7 FL patients.
engagement.judgement: Opening entry for the system the class went into patients on. No animal efficacy or PD model was filed: a grep of the FDA pharmacology review for xenograft, tumor-bearing or in-vivo efficacy returns nothing, and its primary-pharmacology section is entirely cell lines and primary CLL/FL/MCL cells (pAkt, chemokine secretion, migration, apoptosis). Herman 2010 (https://doi.org/10.1182/blood-2010-02-271171, epub 2010-06-03) is the same system in CLL cells and is the earliest use; Lannutti 2011 (epub 2010-10-19) is cited because it is the paper that covers FL-type cells and the EC50. Idelalisib is CAL-101, so product_in_model is true.

engagement.model: Patient B-cell tumour samples and B-cell lines ex vivo
engagement.note: The chemokines CAL-101 suppressed in co-culture (CCL3, CCL4, CXCL13) fell in dosed CLL patients; the paper states the comparison itself.
engagement.quote: These results are corroborated by clinical data showing marked reductions in circulating CCL3, CCL4, and CXCL13 levels, and a surge in lymphocytosis during CAL-101 treatment.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. The dosed humans are CLL patients from the phase 1 (NCT00710528), not FL patients; the brief lets any dosed human count for engagement. No FL-patient PD read-out was found: Flinn 2014 (iNHL phase 1, https://doi.org/10.1182/blood-2013-11-538546) and Gopal 2014 report no pAkt or chemokine data in their abstracts.
engagement.reason: Chemokine read-out moved in dosed patients
engagement.magnitude_basis: plasma CCL3/CCL4/CXCL13 fall in patients vs co-culture secretion block; no ratio computed
engagement.judgement: Chemokines secreted downstream of BCR/PI3Kδ signalling are a downstream read-out, not the kinase's own product (PIP3). The FDA clinical pharmacology review (2014, http://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2014/205858Orig1s000ClinPharmR.pdf) adds the proximal-looking read-out in the same CLL population, also matched: 'On days 8 and 28, constitutive phosphorylation of Akt in cells from patients with CLL was reduced to the background level of healthy subjects.' That does not change the status so it is not a separate entry. The ex-vivo prediction was a direction, so magnitude is direction_only. Registry record NCT00710528 carries no results posting for this PD; registry_date left null.

dose.model: Patient B-cell tumour samples and B-cell lines ex vivo
dose.note: Cell-based potency (EC50 8 nM; EC90 ~301 nM in the FDA review) was the only exposure target; no animal PK/PD model existed.
dose.short: Cell EC50 8 nM was the only target
dose.quote: We thus identified 5-fluoro-3-phenyl-2-[(S)-1-(9H-purin-6-ylamino)-propyl]-3H-quinazolin-4-one (CAL-101), a highly selective and potent p110δ small molecule inhibitor (half-maximal effective concentration [EC(50)] = 8nM).
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the FDA review gives the cell-based EC50 as 8.9 nM and the EC90 as ~125 ng/mL (301 nM, study PC-312-2009).
dose.judgement: Opening entry. The 150 mg BID dose was chosen in the clinic (phase 1 101-02, NCT00710528) from an exposure-tumour-shrinkage plateau; the ex-vivo EC90 is what FDA later checked trough concentrations against. The rat and dog toxicology stated no tolerability margin that carried into dose selection (MTD not reached in patients, MAD 350 mg BID), so margin_stated is null.

dose.model: Patient B-cell tumour samples and B-cell lines ex vivo
dose.note: FDA: at 150 mg BID most iNHL and CLL patients held troughs above the in-vitro PI3Kδ EC90 (>85% on day 28), and the drug worked.
dose.quote: In these trials most patients administered a dose of 150 mg BID achieved minimal concentrations (Ctau) greater than the in vitro EC90 for PI3Kδ inhibition.
dose.confidence_note: Review text grepped and the dose-selection section read in full; the review reports the fraction of patients above EC90 (87% at 150 mg BID in 101-02; >85% on day 28 in 101-09), not a median trough:EC90 ratio, so no magnitude is computed.
dose.judgement: Reached and the drug worked (ORR 57% in 101-09), so 'same'. Two caveats recorded, neither changes the status: the review found no exposure-response relationship for ORR, so exceeding the EC90 is a reached target, not a demonstrated causal threshold; and the toxic end of the window was set clinically, not by a model (the review: 'A higher starting dose is not recommended as idelalisib is associated with hepatotoxicity'). registry_date is the results posting for the FL trial 101-09 (NCT01282424, 2014-09-04); the dose-finding trial 101-02 (NCT00710528) has no results posting. The review reference ID is 3503870 (2014); the NDA was approved 2014-07-23.

dose.confidence_note: Open-access full text read (PMC9132770). The inhibitors dosed were AMG319 and PI-3065, neither a member, so product_in_model is false.
dose.note: Intermittent PI3Kδi (4 days on, 3 off) in tumour-bearing mice kept tumour control without colonic TH17/TC17 expansion; the regimen prediction for the class.
dose.quote: A modified treatment regimen with intermittent dosing of PI3Kδi in mouse models led to a significant decrease in tumour growth without inducing pathogenic T cells in colonic tissue, indicating that alternative dosing regimens might limit toxicity.
dose.judgement: Opening entry at first use. A different system from the D910A kinase-dead mouse (pharmacological, dosed, tumour-bearing; regimen as the variable) and a different prediction (a drug holiday uncouples anti-tumour effect from colitis), so its own track. model_filed is false: the 2014 idelalisib review predates it and no FDA review of zandelisib exists (NDA withdrawn 2022).
dose.model: Mouse PI3Kδ-inhibitor colitis and intermittent-dosing model (B16F10-OVA tumour and DSS colitis; AMG319, PI-3065)

dose.magnitude_basis: any grade 3-4 AE 44% vs 76% intermittent vs continuous in patients; mouse colitis score and colonic TH17/TC17 fraction; no common quantity
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of Pagel 2022 (full text not open). Trial population is mixed FL/CLL B-cell malignancy; dose cells carry no 80% rule. Colitis itself was 3% on both schedules; diarrhoea 5% vs 21% and pneumonia 2% vs 16% carried the difference.
dose.note: Zandelisib phase 1b (run 2016-2020): intermittent dosing cut grade 3-4 AEs to 44% from 76% on continuous dosing; the mouse came after.
dose.quote: 26 (44%) of 59 patients in the intermittent dosing group and 29 (76%) of 38 patients in the continuous dosing group had grade 3-4 adverse events.
dose.judgement: Retrodiction, not a prediction: zandelisib's intermittent cohorts (2018-2020) and TIDAL's regimen (registered 2018-12-07) were set from phase 1b irAEs and a Treg-repopulation rationale, years before the mouse (epub 2022-05-04); the tier-1 trial record (Pagel, epub 2022-07-11) came two months after it, so the comparison was public in 2022. The mouse reproduced the direction (fewer immune AEs on a drug holiday with activity kept: 11/12 responses at 60 mg), so retro, never same. Not a complete reproduction: colitis was 3% on both schedules. margin_stated true because the mouse stated the intermittent regimen was both effective and tolerated. Eschweiler does not cite zandelisib (grep ME-401/zandelisib in the full text: none), so the pairing is mine. NCT02914938 has no results posting.
dose.model: Mouse PI3Kδ-inhibitor colitis and intermittent-dosing model (B16F10-OVA tumour and DSS colitis; AMG319, PI-3065)

dose.magnitude_basis: grade 3-4 colitis 3% on intermittent zandelisib vs 14% on continuous idelalisib (label 2014); mouse gave colitis scores, no ratio
dose.confidence_note: Open-access full text read (PMC11302793); it cites no mouse model (grep Eschweiler/mouse/murine: none). Single-arm, no continuous-dosing comparator inside the trial; the idelalisib label's 14% grade >=3 colitis is the external bar.
dose.note: TIDAL, read after the mouse: zandelisib 7-of-28-day dosing in FL gave ORR 73% with grade 3-4 colitis 3% and diarrhoea 6%.
dose.quote: The intermittent dosing resulted in a relatively low incidence of severe class-related toxicities, which supports the evaluation of zandelisib as a single agent and in combination with indolent B-cell malignancies.
dose.reason: Drug holiday kept efficacy, spared colon
dose.judgement: Decision 10: the first patient result public after the retrodiction is a fresh entry scored as usual. TIDAL's result (registry 2024-02-01) post-dates the mouse (2022-05), so the regimen prediction is compared prospectively, but TIDAL was not designed on it; the sponsor's stated rationale is Treg repopulation during the 21-day break. Regimen target reached (60 mg daily, 7 of 28 days after 8 weeks continuous) and the primary ORR met, so same. Idelalisib's 14% grade >=3 colitis (label 2014) is the continuous-dosing comparator; zandelisib's own continuous arm (Pagel) had 3% colitis, so the colitis reduction is cross-drug and the diarrhoea/pneumonia reduction within-drug. The programme's 2022 discontinuation after the ODAC does not bear on the regimen comparison.
dose.model: Mouse PI3Kδ-inhibitor colitis and intermittent-dosing model (B16F10-OVA tumour and DSS colitis; AMG319, PI-3065)

dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. No FDA review of zandelisib exists (the 2022 NDA was withdrawn before action), so model_filed is unknown.
dose.note: ME-401 reached tumour concentrations 20-30x plasma with slow target dissociation (KD 30 pM), idelalisib 3x and gone by 24 h: the member's own exposure model.
dose.quote: Oral administration of ME-401 in an A20 syngeneic mouse model resulted in tumor concentrations 20-30 times higher than plasma concentrations at 4 h after the last dose.
dose.judgement: Opening entry; Europe PMC gives only the print date (2019-10-01). The paper's own purpose statement is retrospective ('to investigate the basis of the clinical activity of ME-401'), so the comparison it states is scored as a retrodiction in the next entry.
dose.model: A20 syngeneic mouse B-cell lymphoma tissue-distribution and enzyme-binding model (ME-401 vs idelalisib)

dose.magnitude_basis: tumour:plasma ratio and KD in mice vs clinical response rate; no shared quantity
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. The clinical potency it invokes was conference data in 2019; the tier-1 record of that trial is Pagel 2022 (https://doi.org/10.1016/S1470-2045(22)00333-3; NCT02914938, no results posted). The paper gives no exposure target or regimen, so the dose cell has nothing quantitative to check.
dose.note: The paper reads the mouse against clinical potency already seen in the phase 1b (60 mg: 11/12 responses), a retrodiction by its own framing.
dose.quote: These characteristics underlie the high clinical potency seen in B-cell malignancies that may differentiate ME-401 from other PI3Kδ inhibitors currently approved or in development.
dose.reason: Explains potency seen; regimen not derived
dose.judgement: Retro, not same: the model was run to explain activity the sponsor had already seen (phase 1b opened 2016-11; the paper's objective is 'the basis of the clinical activity'). Zandelisib's intermittent regimen was not derived from this model: Zelenetz 2024 bases the 60 mg dose on healthy-volunteer basophil-activation IC90 troughs and the 21-day break on plasma clearance plus Treg repopulation, and cites neither this paper nor tumour retention (grep of the full text: none). So no prospective TIDAL entry is added on this track; the regimen is scored on the Eschweiler and basophil tracks.
dose.model: A20 syngeneic mouse B-cell lymphoma tissue-distribution and enzyme-binding model (ME-401 vs idelalisib)

dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (Clin Ther, paywalled). The study pre-dates the first-in-patient trial (opened 2016-11-17), so 2018 is the publication year, a late proxy for first use.
dose.note: Single ascending doses 10-150 mg in healthy men, with ex-vivo basophil activation as the PI3Kδ read-out; this assay set zandelisib's IC90 exposure target.
dose.quote: Blood was drawn at various time points to analyze plasma concentrations of ME-401 and inhibition of basophil activation, a marker of phosphatidylinositol 3 kinase p110δ inhibition.
dose.judgement: Opening entry. A human ex-vivo PD system, not the draft's patient B-cell EC90 track: different drug, different cells (whole-blood basophils of dosed volunteers) and a prospective exposure target rather than FDA's post-hoc check. No engagement entry: the readout moved in the volunteers who are the model, so there is no separate patient comparison to score.
dose.model: Healthy-volunteer whole-blood basophil activation test (ex-vivo PI3Kδ PD assay for ME-401 dose setting)

dose.confidence_note: Open-access full text read. The trial reports no patient trough data, so 'reached' rests on the healthy-volunteer PK the paper cites; Pagel 2022 (no DLT to 180 mg, activity similar across 60-180 mg) is the dose-finding record, abstract only.
dose.note: Zelenetz states it: 60 mg daily keeps troughs above the basophil-test IC90; at that dose TIDAL met its primary ORR (73%).
dose.quote: A single ascending dose study evaluating zandelisib in healthy volunteers established that 60 mg daily achieves trough plasma concentrations exceeding the IC90 for PI3Kδ inhibition in the basophil activation test.
dose.judgement: Reached and the drug worked (primary ORR 73%, CR 38%), so same. margin_stated false: the single-dose study stated no chronic tolerability margin, and the irAEs that forced the intermittent schedule are scored on the Treg and colitis tracks, not here. Year 2024 is the first tier-1 statement of the comparison (TIDAL registry results 2024-02-01, paper epub 2024-08-06); Pagel 2022 is earlier for the dose but its abstract does not state the basophil IC90 link.
dose.model: Healthy-volunteer whole-blood basophil activation test (ex-vivo PI3Kδ PD assay for ME-401 dose setting)

efficacy.model: Patient B-cell tumour samples and B-cell lines ex vivo
efficacy.note: Apoptosis of B-cell lines and primary patient samples, including FL biopsy cells, was the whole efficacy case; no FL xenograft or mouse lymphoma was run.
efficacy.short: Apoptosis in patient B cells; no animal
efficacy.quote: These effects have been observed across a broad range of immature and mature B-cell malignancies, thereby providing a rationale for the ongoing clinical evaluation of CAL-101.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the FL-specific datum is in the FDA pharmacology review: 'Idelalisib, at a concentration of 0.1 µM, inhibited P-AKT (Ser473) an average of 86% (range 55-97%) in malignant B-cells prepared from biopsy specimens of 7 patients with follicular lymphoma.'
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry. The FDA review names p110δ over-expression in FL-derived lines (WSU-FSCCL, WSU-NHL) and apoptosis in malignant B cells as the pharmacology basis; no in-vivo tumour model appears anywhere in the review (grep for xenograft / tumor model / in vivo efficacy: none). The cell is therefore not empty: a model (ex-vivo cells) was relied on.

efficacy.model: Patient B-cell tumour samples and B-cell lines ex vivo
efficacy.note: Single-arm 101-09 met its primary endpoint: ORR 57% in iNHL, 54% (39/72) in FL; the apoptosis-in-patient-cells prediction held in direction.
efficacy.quote: The response rate was 57% (71 of 125 patients), with 6% meeting the criteria for a complete response.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of Gopal 2014; the FL-specific ORR (54%, 39 of 72) is from the FDA medical review of NDA 205858 (http://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2014/205858Orig1s000MedR.pdf). FL was 58% of the trial, below the 80% bar, so the FL subgroup number is what scores.
efficacy.reason: Primary ORR met; later drugs agree
efficacy.magnitude_basis: ex-vivo apoptosis predicts activity, not a response rate; ORR 54% in FL is a direction match only

patient_trials.quote: The response rate was 57% (71 of 125 patients), with 6% meeting the criteria for a complete response.
The ORR was 73% (95% confidence interval [CI], 63.9-80.4), the complete response (CR) rate was 38% (95% CI, 29.3-47.3), and the median DOR was 16.4 months (95% CI, 9.5-not reached).

efficacy.judgement: Gopal 2014 cites the pathway rationale but never sets the cell data beside the trial, so this is my pairing (comparison_stated false, model_src Lannutti 2011). Status is 'same', not 'neg': no member has failed an FL efficacy endpoint for the model to have flagged. Zandelisib (TIDAL, NCT03768505, results posted 2024-02-01; Zelenetz 2024) matched with ORR 73%; linperlisib's China phase 2 (Clin Cancer Res 2023, https://doi.org/10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-22-2939; NCT04370405, no results posted) was verified by title only, not read. What later went wrong was not the model's prediction: (1) the two randomized confirmatory iNHL trials (NCT01732913 R±idelalisib, NCT01732926 BR±idelalisib) were terminated in 2016 for infection deaths (registry status TERMINATED, results posted 2017-05-11) before PFS could verify benefit, so outcome_tested stays null rather than negative; (2) FDA withdrew the FL and SLL indications effective 2022-05-26 (Federal Register 2022-11277: 'On January 10, 2022, Gilead submitted a letter requesting withdrawal of the follicular lymphoma indication and the SLL indication for ZYDELIG (idelalisib) Tablets and waiving its opportunity for a hearing.') because the accelerated-approval confirmation was never delivered; (3) zandelisib's single-arm filing was refused in 2022 and the program discontinued (Zelenetz 2024: 'While zandelisib clinical program was discontinued due to regulatory challenges...'), after the April 2022 ODAC on PI3K inhibitors raised the bar to randomized trials with overall-survival data. Copanlisib, duvelisib and umbralisib, whose randomized trials drove that ODAC, are not members and are not scored. Rule 7: the 2014 status stands on what was known in 2014.

safety.note: Mice with catalytically dead p110δ had blunted B- and T-cell responses and spontaneous inflammatory bowel disease: the genetic forecast of on-target colitis and immunosuppression.
safety.quote: Antigen receptor signaling in B and T cells was impaired and immune responses in vivo were attenuated in p110delta mutant mice. They also developed inflammatory bowel disease.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of Okkenhaug 2002, Patton 2006 and Uno 2010.
safety.judgement: A separate track from the rat/dog toxicology: a different system (genetic inactivation of the target, no drug, product_in_model false) making a different prediction (immune-mediated inflammation from loss of p110δ in regulatory T cells rather than chemical organ toxicity). The mechanism was made explicit before the clinic: Patton 2006 (https://doi.org/10.4049/jimmunol.177.10.6598): 'In adoptive transfer experiments, p110deltaD910A/D910A T cells failed to protect against experimental colitis.'; Uno 2010 (https://doi.org/10.1053/j.gastro.2010.07.008) characterised the spontaneous colitis. The model was not in the FDA pharmacology review (grep for kinase-dead, knock-in, Treg, regulatory T: none), so model_filed is false.

safety.note: Rats and dogs on idelalisib showed liver enzyme rises with inflammation and necrosis, GI ulceration and inflammation, lung infiltrates, lymphoid depletion, cardiomyopathy and pancreatitis.
safety.short: Rat/dog: liver, GI, lung, heart harm
safety.quote: Idelalisib-related toxicities in rats and dogs included findings in the following organs: liver (increased ALT, AST, and GGT, inflammation, and necrosis), heart (cardiomyopathy, inflammation, and fibrosis), pancreas (inflammation and low incidence acinar degeneration), lung (infiltration, alveolar macrophages)
safety.confidence_note: Year is a proxy: the 28-day rat and dog studies are undated in the review text I grepped, and IND-enabling toxicology precedes the 2008 first-in-human trial (NCT00710528, first posted 2008-07). The review itself is dated 2014.
safety.judgement: Opening entry for the filed toxicology track, kept apart from the kinase-dead mouse because it is a different system with a different prediction (direct organ toxicity of the molecule, including off-target or metabolite effects). Review: 28-day rat and dog, 13-week and 6-month rat, 9-month dog studies; the 9-month dog deaths were attributed to systemic inflammation 'with no signs of hepatotoxicity in this study'.

safety.note: Severe diarrhea/colitis in 14% and serious hepatotoxicity in 14% of patients, both immune-mediated, as loss of p110δ in Treg cells foretold; infections followed in 2016.
safety.short: Immune colitis in 14% as mouse foretold
safety.quote: Severe diarrhea or colitis (Grade 3 or higher) occurred in 14% of Zydelig-treated patients.
safety.confidence_note: The label pools iNHL and CLL patients; it does not cite the mouse (comparison_stated false, pairing by me). The immune mechanism in patients comes from Lampson 2016 in front-line CLL (abstract-level), not from FL patients.
safety.reason: Colitis and Treg loss as predicted
safety.magnitude_basis: colitis present/absent; incidence in mice (spontaneous, age-dependent) and patients (14% grade ≥3) not comparable
safety.judgement: The classic PI3Kδ safety comparison. The mouse's stated prediction (immune colitis, attenuated immunity) held: (1) colitis, label 2014, with idelalisib-associated colitis later shown histologically to be a lymphocytic, autoimmune-like enterocolitis; (2) hepatotoxicity proved immune-mediated with the predicted Treg loss, Lampson 2016 (https://doi.org/10.1182/blood-2016-03-707133, epub 2016-05-31, front-line CLL, MONDO:0004948): 'A decrease in peripheral blood regulatory T cells was seen in patients experiencing toxicity on therapy, which is consistent with an immune-mediated mechanism.'; Chellappa 2019 (https://doi.org/10.4049/jimmunol.1701703) then showed idelalisib preferentially inhibits human Treg function (title verified, not read); (3) the 2016 safety holds: EMA's Article 20 referral (started 2016-03-17, CHMP opinion 2016-07-21, https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/medicines/human/referrals/zydelig): 'Increased rates of serious adverse effects including deaths were seen in the treatment arm of 3 clinical trials' in first-line CLL and relapsed iNHL, 'The additional deaths were mainly caused by infections' (Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia, CMV), which is the mouse's attenuated immunity; the FDA's 2016-03-14 communication (Gilead stopped six combination trials) is no longer at its URL and was not re-read. None of these changes the status, so they are not separate entries. What the mouse did not show: hepatitis and pneumonitis as organs. Those are scored on the toxicology track, which saw liver and lung findings, so the harm is counted once. Zandelisib's intermittent schedule was designed on this Treg mechanism to spare the immune toxicities (Zelenetz 2024: grade 3-4 colitis 3%, AST elevation 2%), a later use of the same prediction.

safety.note: FDA set the species beside patients: liver enzymes, GI and rash matched; lung infiltrates matched pneumonitis; rat cardiomyopathy and pancreatitis never appeared.
safety.short: Liver, GI, lung held; heart did not
safety.quote: In patients treated with ZYDELIG, liver toxicity (characterized by increased ALT, AST, and GGT), GI disturbance, and skin rash have been reported.
safety.confidence_note: Review executive summary read in full; the label's section 13.2 states the partial match explicitly.
safety.reason: Liver, GI, lung matched; heart over-predicted
safety.magnitude_basis: organ-by-organ presence: liver, GI, lung, lymphoid depletion held; cardiac and pancreatic did not
safety.judgement: The regulator states the comparison in both directions. Held: liver (boxed warning, fatal/serious hepatotoxicity 14%), GI (severe diarrhea/colitis 14%, intestinal perforation), rash, lung (rat/dog infiltrates and alveolar macrophages; patient pneumonitis 3.6-5.4% in the CLL review), lymphoid depletion (2016 infection deaths). Not held, by the label's own words (section 13.2): 'Toxicities observed in animals and not reported in patients include cardiac toxicity (cardiomyopathy, inflammation, and increased heart weight) and pancreatic findings (inflammation, hemorrhage, and low-incidence acinar degeneration and hyperplasia).' I score the track 'same' with source_calls_it 'partial' rather than 'contra' with magnitude 'opposite' because the regulator itself calls the comparison a partial match and the harms that defined the drug's label were the ones the species showed; the cardiac over-prediction is recorded here so a stricter re-score can flip it. The label places the rat cardiac and pancreatic findings 'at exposures (AUCs) higher than those reported in patients at the recommended dose of 150 mg twice daily', without a multiple, so the over-prediction is at supra-clinical exposure and I do not treat it as an independent wrong prediction at the clinical dose. Pneumonitis is counted here, not on the kinase-dead track, because this is the system that showed lung findings.

safety.confidence_note: Open-access full text read. 'Treg' carries a subscript 'reg' in the source; otherwise verbatim.
safety.note: Dosed PI3Kδi depleted colonic ST2 Treg cells, expanded TH17/TC17 cells and worsened DSS colitis in mice: a mechanism for the class's colitis.
safety.short: Dosed mice lose colonic Tregs, get colitis
safety.quote: Accordingly, in mouse models, PI3Kδi decreased the number of Treg cells systemically and caused colitis.
safety.judgement: Opening entry. Kept apart from the D910A kinase-dead mouse: that is genetic loss from birth with spontaneous colitis; this is a dosed inhibitor in adult tumour-bearing or DSS-challenged mice with single-cell resolution of which Treg subset is lost. Same organ, different system, and the regimen prediction it adds is scored on dose.
safety.model: Mouse PI3Kδ-inhibitor colitis and intermittent-dosing model (B16F10-OVA tumour and DSS colitis; AMG319, PI-3065)

safety.magnitude_basis: colitis present in dosed mice vs 14% grade >=3 colitis on idelalisib; no incidence ratio
safety.confidence_note: The paper's own dosed patients are AMG319 head-and-neck cancer patients (EudraCT 2014-004388-20); AMG319 is not a member and does not score. The scoring patient side is idelalisib's colitis, cited by the paper as refs 1-2 (Furman 2014, Gopal 2014) and on the 2014 label. 'Treg' subscript as above.
safety.note: The paper sets its mouse beside PI3Kδi-treated patients (idelalisib refs 1-2; AMG319 12/21 irAE discontinuations), reproducing the colitis known since the 2014 label.
safety.quote: Together, these findings suggest a heightened sensitivity of certain colonic Treg subsets to PI3Kδi, potentially related to the high incidence of colitis observed in patients treated with PI3Kδi.
safety.judgement: A retrodiction: idelalisib's colitis was on the label (2014) and shown immune-mediated (Lampson 2016, the paper's ref 6) before this mouse was run, so retro, never same. The statement compares the model with PI3Kδi patients generally, with idelalisib's FL and CLL trials as the cited class record, so imported_from stays null; the AMG319 solid-tumour patients are context only. The harm is counted once: the D910A track scores colitis prospectively; this track records that a dosed model reproduces it with a Treg-subset mechanism.
safety.model: Mouse PI3Kδ-inhibitor colitis and intermittent-dosing model (B16F10-OVA tumour and DSS colitis; AMG319, PI-3065)

safety.confidence_note: Author manuscript full text read (PMC6387453). Sogkas 2018 (https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jaci.2018.06.039, epub 2018-07-21) reported PIK3CD deficiency three months earlier; title verified, text not read, so the track opens on Cohen.
safety.note: A patient expressing kinase-dead p110δ (D853Gfs) had combined immunodeficiency and recurrent colitis: the human genetic counterpart of the D910A mouse.
safety.quote: Here, we report an immunodeficiency due to a kinase-dead PI3Kδ mutant, illustrating the importance of p110δ catalytic activity in adaptive immunity.
safety.judgement: Opening entry at first use of this system (the checker's lead). An earlier kindred with a contiguous PIK3CD/SKAP deletion (2013, cited by Cohen as 'the previously reported kindred lacking p110δ expression') is a dual-gene loss and is not used.
safety.model: People with loss-of-function PIK3CD genotypes (kinase-dead or null p110δ)

safety.magnitude_basis: colitis in 3 of 4 loss-of-function carriers vs 14% grade >=3 colitis on idelalisib; no common denominator
safety.confidence_note: Author manuscript read; 'p110δD910A' carries a superscript in the source. Swan 2019 (Haematologica, https://doi.org/10.3324/haematol.2018.208397, epub 2019-05-09) adds a null-PIK3CD patient with enterocolitis and states the comparison: 'In humans, immune dysregulation including severe colitis is present in many cancer patients who are treated with the p110δ-specific inhibitor idelalisib.' No status change, so not a separate entry.
safety.note: Cohen states it: D910A mice and three of four reported PIK3CD loss-of-function patients share colitis susceptibility, the adverse effect of p110δ inhibitors.
safety.short: LoF carriers share the inhibitor colitis
safety.quote: The p110δD910A mice as well as three of the four previously reported patients with LOF variants in PIK3CD have susceptibility to colitis, which is also a potential adverse effect associated with p110δ inhibitors used to treat solid and hematopoietic malignancies.
safety.judgement: A human genotype reported four years after the 2014 label is a retrodiction by construction, so retro. Cohen calls the match partial in the next sentence ('colitis is not a universal feature shared by all patients with LOF PIK3CD variants or p110δ inhibition, and has not been reported in Pik3cd-/- mice'), hence source_calls_it partial. The genotype also reproduces the infection susceptibility (two of five carriers died of sepsis) behind the 2016 idelalisib infection deaths. Separate track from the D910A mouse: same prediction, different species and system.
safety.model: People with loss-of-function PIK3CD genotypes (kinase-dead or null p110δ)

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the IC50s are in the abstract.
safety.note: Idelalisib inhibited human Treg proliferation at IC50 0.5 uM versus 2.0 uM (CD4) and 6.5 uM (CD8) effectors and cut Treg suppression.
safety.quote: On this background, we examined the effect of idelalisib on the function of human Tregs ex vivo with respect to proliferation, TCR signaling, phenotype, and suppressive function.
safety.judgement: Opening entry. A different system from the draft's ex-vivo B-cell track (healthy-donor T cells, not patient tumour cells) with a different prediction (Treg-selective inhibition breaks tolerance), and from the D910A mouse (human cells, the product itself), so its own track.
safety.model: Human regulatory T-cell ex-vivo suppression and proliferation assay (idelalisib on healthy-donor Treg vs effector T cells)

safety.magnitude_basis: Treg IC50 0.5 uM vs effector 2.0-6.5 uM ex vivo; patient Treg phenotype shift, no ratio
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the number of patients phenotyped and their trial are not in the abstract, so registry_date is null. Patients are CLL, imported.
safety.note: Treg phenotyping of idelalisib-treated CLL patients matched the ex-vivo Treg-preferential inhibition; the assay was built after the autoimmune toxicities were known.
safety.quote: Phenotyping Tregs from CLL patients treated with idelalisib supported our in vitro findings.
safety.reason: Treg loss reproduced in dosed patients
safety.judgement: The paper says the assay was motivated by idelalisib's autoimmune adverse effects ('On this background'), so it is a retrodiction and scores retro. The patient side is CLL (imported_from MONDO:0004948); the FL label pools the same colitis and hepatitis. It supplies the mechanism (Treg loss) that the draft's D910A entry already cites from Lampson 2016, without changing that track.
safety.model: Human regulatory T-cell ex-vivo suppression and proliferation assay (idelalisib on healthy-donor Treg vs effector T cells)
